title: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal (LOTO, side panel access, valve cover removal, M8 connector disconnect)
summary: Perform LOTO on the OptiSweep tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor/valve area, remove the valve cover secured by four M4x50 socket-head screws, and disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the pneumatic valve.
when_to_use: Use when removing the pneumatic valve at the OptiSweep tipper station requires LOTO, side panel access, valve cover removal, and disconnecting the valve’s M8 electrical connector (as part of the pneumatic valve replacement/removal task).
not_for: Do not continue if the station side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.
Do not continue if the M8 electrical connector cannot be disconnected from the edge of the valve.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Execute LOTO and perform the physical removal/disconnection steps (side panel, valve cover screws, and M8 connector).
safety_notes: Apply LOTO to the tipper before starting the removal steps.
access_or_tools_needed: Tools: 2.5-mm hex wrench, 3-mm hex wrench, 5-mm hex wrench, 6-mm hex wrench, 3/8-in. wrench or socket, Loctite®
LOTO capability for the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2)

access_required: On-site physical access to the OptiSweep tipper station side panel and valve cover area
system_preconditions: Tipper is capable of being LOTO’d

visual_references.description: Figure 7-9 pneumatic valve maintenance diagram showing valve cover, four M4x50 socket-head screws, and M8 connector location on the valve edge.

steps.title: LOTO the tipper
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely locked out before accessing the motor/valve area.
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO on the tipper (use the lockout/tagout reference labeled "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).
steps.healthy_condition: Tipper remains in a locked-out state while you proceed to physical removal steps.
steps.failure_condition: You begin side panel/valve cover removal without the tipper being LOTO’d.

actions.label: Apply LOTO to tipper
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal: Step 1. LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

steps.title: Remove station side panel (if necessary) to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the motor/valve area by removing the station side panel when required.
steps.instruction: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (or remains in place if not necessary) and the motor access area is available.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine (9) self-tapping securing screws are removed before attempting to remove the side panel.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.

actions.label: Check whether side panel removal is necessary
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws, stop and re-check that all securing screws are removed before continuing.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal: Step 2. If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Remove valve cover screws
steps.purpose: Release the valve cover so the valve and its electrical connector can be accessed.
steps.instruction: Remove the four (4) M4 socket head screws holding the valve cover in place.
steps.expected_result: Valve cover is no longer secured by the four (4) M4 socket head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: All four (4) M4 socket head screws are removed from the valve cover.
steps.failure_condition: Valve cover remains secured because one or more of the four (4) M4 socket head screws are still installed.

actions.label: Remove valve cover screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the four (4) M4 socket head screws holding the valve cover in place.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal: Step 3. Remove the four (4) M4 socket head screws holding the valve cover in place. Figure 7-9 shows VALVE COVER and M4x50 socket-head screws.

steps.title: Disconnect M8 electrical connector from valve edge
steps.purpose: Disconnect the valve’s electrical connection to complete the removal/disconnection portion of the pneumatic valve removal task.
steps.instruction: Disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the valve.
steps.expected_result: The M8 electrical connector has been disconnected from the edge of the pneumatic valve.
steps.healthy_condition: Connector is fully disengaged from the valve edge (no retention still engaged).
steps.failure_condition: M8 electrical connector cannot be disconnected from the edge of the valve.

actions.label: Disconnect M8 connector
actions.exact_action: Disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the valve.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the M8 electrical connector cannot be disconnected from the edge of the valve, stop and re-check connector seating/retention before applying additional force.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal: Step 4. Disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the valve. Figure 7-9 supports identification of the M8 connector location on the valve edge.

success_criteria: Station side panel is removed when necessary to access the motor/valve area.
Valve cover is no longer secured by the four (4) M4 socket head screws.
M8 electrical connector is disconnected from the edge of the pneumatic valve.
healthy_conditions: All nine (9) self-tapping securing screws are removed before attempting side panel removal.
All four (4) M4 socket head screws are removed from the valve cover.
M8 electrical connector disengages from the valve edge without resistance indicating improper seating/retention.
failure_conditions: Side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.
M8 electrical connector cannot be disconnected from the edge of the valve.
escalation_guidance: If side panel removal or M8 connector disconnection fails as specified in the stop conditions, stop work and re-check the stated screw/connector seating/retention before applying additional force.

screens_or_images.description: Figure 7-9: Pneumatic Valve diagram used to identify valve cover, four M4x50 socket-head screws, and M8 connector location on the valve edge.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal steps 1-4: LOTO the tipper; remove nine (9) self-tapping securing screws to remove station side panel if necessary; remove four (4) M4 socket head screws holding valve cover; disconnect M8 electrical connector from edge of valve.

missing_details: The packet includes LOTO reference by name ("Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2) but does not include the actual LOTO procedure text/steps; operators must use their site’s referenced lockout/tagout procedure for the tipper.
